ex.s: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.

defs.def: a particular group of people 一伙人；一帮人
ordinary people, not special or unusual in any way 群众；民众；老百姓；凡夫俗子

ex.s: It’s lovely at the beach, but not so when you’re wearing a suit and in a crowd of passengers!
ex.t: 在海滩上很好，但当你穿着西装挤在一群乘客中时就不那么好了！

ex.s: And next time you look up at the sky don’t just look for rain crowds, but also for birds.
ex.t: 下次抬头看天空时，不要只寻找雨云，也去寻找鸟群。

ex.s: Look how the crowd has gone wild.

defs.def: to fill a place so there is little room to move 挤满；塞满；使 … 拥挤

ex.s: After Darwin had spent some time in South America, his room on the ship was crowded with samples of the plants and animals he had collected.
ex.t: 达尔文在南美待了一段时间后，他在船上的房间里堆满了他收集的动植物样本。

defs.def: to fill your mind so that you can think of nothing else 涌上（心头）；涌入（脑海）
to stand very close to sb so that they feel uncomfortable or nervous 挤，靠近，挤在一旁（以致使人不舒服或紧张）
